questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country to improve my English, and I have visited Canada in the past and loved it, so I wanted to have the opportunity to see even more of Canada this time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. We were a lot of students from KU, so we helped each other finding information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember receiving any assistance, but I didn't feel that it was necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university was very good if you needed help. I was in contact with my academic advisor in the beginning, as I needed help with enrolling in some of my courses, and that all worked very well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. The housing marked in Hamilton was crazy, and it was very hard for a lot of students to find a reasonable place to live. We were very lucky to find a house 5 minutes walking distance from campus. The landlord wanted to rent to us, even though we were exchange, but a lot of students were struggling with this, and there are a lot of scams there, so it was very difficult to navigate through.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of scams. Don't transfer money before you have seen a house. Some people were even on video calls with "landlords" showing a house and it was still a scam. 
Other than that, the areas Westdale and Ainslie Wood were very nice to live in as students, because there are a lot students living in these areas. The downtown is a bit far from the university, so if possible I would recommend looking into these areas.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
We were lucky with our house, but I know a lot that struggled with finding housing. We didn't find the house before getting to Hamilton. 
A lot of exchange students also living on campus, but that option is a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy. They were very helpful at campus.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think we had to go to the university and grab a student card and had some introduction day as well where they told all things that were important to know.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your academic advisor, the administration, other students and such.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read the mails that they send, it explains most that you need to know in the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a lot easier than I thought it would be.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses with 2nd year and 3rd year economics students. If I wanted to be challenged more I should probably had chosen 3rd and 4th year courses. You can see on the course code what year it is meant for.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different, more interactive than UCPH. You had to participate in lectures and speak in groups and present in the lectures, which is very different from the lectures I know at home, where there is a professor that speaks, and then sometimes questions for the room, but not a lot compared to in Canada.
Also there are midterms, and a lot more test, such that in the end, the final exam only counts for e.g. 30% of the grade. It depends on the course, but in a lot of the courses we had, the final exams that did not count for a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Monetary Economics, Public policy toward business, International Trade, Analysis of Economic data.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Monetary Economics was very very good. The professor was very good at uploading information about the course, you could see it online or in person, she was very thorough and the material that was covered was very interesting for me.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had read on this site before I left for exchange, so all the cost that I encountered were cost I was somewhat aware of.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Phone bill, alcohol, grocery shopping and such were more expensive. Eating out was cheaper than in Copenhagen, but you always had to add a tip and tax to the bill on top of the food, so in total just a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was free gym, and they just made a big new one in December. Also free squash courts. A lot of opportunities to join clubs and work out for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students, almost everything that you could imagine, so they were very good in that department.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Squash was fun. There also very a lot of trips to different parks and stuff, that was fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Algonquin park was amazing! Not far from Hamilton. We rented a car and drove to that a weekend, very fun. Do it in late summer/fall where the leaves turn red, very beautiful. Other than that Montreal was nice, very european. Banff and Jasper in Alberta was amazing, we rented a car and drove through the Rocky Mountains. Vancouver is also nice. In general, very nice to go travelling in Canada, but get an international driving license, and rent a car, it gives a lot of freedom when travelling. Also because the trains and busses are not working as well as in Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, Canadians are really friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the events that the university hosts.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It costs more than you think, go travel a lot, and make sure to attend the events in the beginning an get to know other students (there is a trip in the beginning of the semester called MOOSE that is very good for getting to know a lot of other peers).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling around, meeting a lot of other students from different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not drinking.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
